  "isAccessibleForFree": true,
  "description": "For real binary tensors in the closed Frobenius unit ball, no single additional determinant-polynomial inequality defines the Gram locus when n ≥ 3.",
  "abstract": "For a real tensor with n binary factors, consider the determinants of its one-mode Gram matrices as the tensor ranges over the closed Frobenius unit ball. For every n ≥ 3, this locus cannot be defined by one polynomial nonnegativity condition in the determinant coordinates, even after imposing the cube bounds or the known convex-hull inequalities. This answers Seigal's single-polynomial question negatively for n ≥ 4. The proof combines established qubit marginal polygon inequalities, an explicit real three-factor realization, a multiplicity obstruction, and exact zero-determinant slices. A strictly positive rational counterexample also refutes the proposed polynomial. Our theorem was recorded in a September 30, 2026 GitHub submission. Ferudun's October 2, 2026 preprint gives an overlapping stronger theorem; we credit it and record the chronology without claiming exclusive priority or certifying mutual independence.",
